newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on corn/soybean surge.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on corn/soybean surge.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on a weather-related surge in corn and soybean futures, traders said.
"Weather, weather, weather that's all I can say. I don't have anything pithy to say," said Dave Armstrong, analyst for ABN-Amro The Chicago Corp.

The corn and soybean market was boosted sharply higher Monday on hotter and drier weather over the U.S. Midwest over the weekend and concerns that the pattern may continue. The CBOT December through July corn contracts closed up their 12-cent-per-bushel trading limit.
Dry weather in parts of Australia's wheat growing area also was mentioned but most traders said the gains in wheat were tied solely to the corn and soybean rally.
Wheat closed 2-1/2 to 7-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up seven at $3.29. September was up 6-1/2 at $3.36.

However, the wheat market rally was capped by nearly ideal wheat harvest weather in U.S. winter wheat regions and by reports of excellent wheat yields in the U.S. hard and soft red winter wheat. Gains were also checked by Friday's bearish USDA 1997 U.S. winter wheat production report.

USDA Friday said U.S. winter wheat production this year would total 1.781 billion bushels, above an average of analysts' estimates for 1.687 billion and sharply above the 1996 U.S. winter wheat tally of 1.478 billion.
Dean Witter bought three million bushels of September, Smith Barney bought 1.5 million September and Continental Grain sold four million September, traders said.
In spread trading, ABN Amro, The Chicago Corp did one half million bushels of September/July at 7-1/2 cents, premium September, floor sources said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 24,000 contracts, above the 20,104 traded Friday.
In wheat options, E.D. and F. Man Interntional bought 500 December $3.80 calls at 9-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, below the 5,993 traded Friday.
